assertions.statement: April 3 advance-picket contact is reported in the Chalmers/Craft chain.
assertions.limit: Clanton is a verbal intermediate; captured men are feared, not confirmed. Craft reports incoming information and movements, not a verified arrival or independent witness.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.387; p387-provisional
citations.quote: Colonel Clanton has just reported verbally to me that the enemy's pickets attacked his advance pickets about daylight this morning, and he fears that two of his men were captured, though he was not able to state accurately the facts. As soon as I am accurately informed I will report to you.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.388; p388-update
citations.quote: General Chalmers directs me to inform you that information has just come in that the enemy, supposed to be one regiment, have driven in our pickets on both the Pittsburg and Savannah roads. The general has advanced two regiments up each of these roads, which are now on the march. He has gone himself to direct the advance.

assertions.statement: Grant retrospectively reports skirmishing on April 3 and 4.
assertions.limit: Written April 5; no exact time/place or identification with the Chalmers episodes. Do not merge or count these as additional independent engagements.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.94; p94-grant-earlier
citations.quote: Some skirmishing took place with our outguards and the enemy's yesterday and day before.

assertions.statement: Sherman, Buckland and Ricker report return/retirement from the April 4 encounter.
assertions.limit: Accounts share a reporting chain. End-after-night is Sherman’s report, not a synchronized clock or proof every outpost ceased firing.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.90; p90-return
citations.quote: As soon as I heard artillery I advanced with two regiments of infantry and took position and remained until the scattered companies of infantry and cavalry returned. This was after night.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.91; p91-buckland
citations.quote: The cavalry pursued, and we followed until it was ascertained that the enemy were in force a short distance ahead, when we returned, in company with the cavalry.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.92; p92-ricker-retirement
citations.quote: Colonel Buckland coming up at this time with his command, we formed and retired in good order, bringing off 9 prisoners.

assertions.statement: Hardee reports Clanton retiring and a repulse near the Confederate infantry/artillery on April 4.
assertions.limit: The sides describe an overlapping encounter differently. No new casualty, strength or exact position is admitted.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.93; p93-letter
citations.quote:
CAMP NEAR MICKEY'S, April 4, 1862.

GENERAL: The cavalry and infantry of the enemy attacked Colonel Clanton's regiment, which was posted, as I before informed you, about 500 or 600 yards in advance of my lines. Colonel Clanton retired, and the enemy's cavalry followed until they came near our infantry and artillery, when they were gallantly repulsed with slight loss.

assertions.statement: April 4 correspondence stages the advance and changes the next morning’s movement; Polk explicitly acknowledges the order.
assertions.limit: Order, intent and recipient acknowledgment are different from execution. No 3 a.m. actual departure is inferred; Jordan’s earlier same-page message refers to a changed reserve movement, not this identical order.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.390; p390-johnston
citations.quote: General Hardee and Generals Polk and Bragg are approaching positions assigned to them in their destination for the first day's march, which they will hold till reserve reaches Monterey.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.391; p391-bragg
citations.quote: These delays will render it necessary to hold General Hardee in check until we can be ready in the rear. I shall take the liberty of sending this information to him, and direct him to hold up until he hears of my force being in position.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.391; p391-jordan-revision
citations.quote: The commanding general directs me to say, on reflection, he wishes you to march promptly with your command at 3 o'clock in the morning in support of the movement ordered to be made at that hour by Generals Hardee and Bragg. It is of the utmost importance for the success of this movement that your troops shall move precisely at the time designated.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.392; p392-polk-receipt
citations.quote: Your note changing my orders and directing me to move at 3 o'clock on to-morrow morning in support of the forward movement under Generals Hardee and Bragg is received. My corps is in the position assigned it, and will move promptly at the hour appointed.

assertions.statement: Hardee’s February 7, 1863 report describes April 4 bivouac, renewed movement on April 5, and postponement of the general attack.
assertions.limit: A retrospective account, not an April 1862 order. Hardee expressly warns about accuracy after the lapse of time; timings and geography are not adjudicated.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.567; p567-bivouac
citations.quote: The Third Corps, under my command, marched in advance by the Bark road toward Shiloh, and reached Mickey's house, about 16 miles from Corinth and 8 from Pittsburg, on the morning of April 4. A portion of Brigadier-General Cleburne's command in the afternoon engaged the cavalry of the enemy and repulsed it promptly. We took some prisoners and bivouacked for the night.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.567; p567-renewal
citations.quote: It was the purpose of the general to continue the movement at 3 a. m. the succeeding morning, but torrents of rain having fallen, a night march over the swollen streams and flooded ravines became impracticable. The advance was suspended until dawn, when my command again marched forward.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.567; p567-postponement
citations.quote: The storm of the preceding night rendered the roads so miry that the different commands were not collected at Shiloh until 4 or 5 o’clock in the afternoon. This rendered it necessary to postpone the attack until the next day.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.571; p571-caveat
citations.quote: I fear that it may do unintentional injustice; but I trust that my brave associates in arms will appreciate the difficulties of exact accuracy after such a lapse of time, and that you, general, will accord me indulgence for any imperfections it may contain.

assertions.statement: Wood reports no Saturday advance by his brigade, a night picket deployment and Sunday firing; Hardee links Sunday skirmish contact to his advance.
assertions.limit: Wood’s statement is brigade-specific and does not disprove another Saturday encounter. His 5 o’clock and Hardee’s dawn wording do not settle the rival first-contact clocks.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.591; p591-saturday
citations.quote: No advance occurred on Saturday. Major Hardcastle's battalion was thrown out 400 yards in advance, on picket duty, during the night; Colonel McKoin in rear as reserve.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.591; p591-sunday
citations.quote: We slept on our arms in line of battle on Saturday night. As early as 5 o'clock Sunday morning firing occurred between our pickets and the enemy. I sent Captain Clare, of my staff, to instruct Major Hardcastle to hold his position until the brigade came up. The order was faithfully carried out and executed.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.568; p568-sunday
citations.quote: The order was given to advance at daylight on Sunday, April 6. The morning was bright and bracing. At early dawn the enemy attacked the skirmishers in front of my line, commanded by Major (now Colonel) Hardcastle, which was handsomely resisted by that promising young officer. My command advanced, and in half an hour the battle became fierce.

assertions.statement: Sherman reports his lines quiet and expresses an expectation against a general attack on April 5.
assertions.limit: Local observation and belief, not proof no fighting occurred elsewhere or later that Saturday. The prior Grant note is marked Not found by the compiler on p.93.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.93; p93-sherman-quiet
citations.quote: All is quiet along my lines now.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 2, printed p.94; p94-sherman-expectation
citations.quote: The enemy is saucy, but got the worst of it yesterday, and will not press our pickets far. I will not be drawn out far unless with certainty of advantage, and I do not apprehend anything like an attack on our position.

assertions.statement: The later Official Records catalog distinguishes April 4 skirmish from April 6–7 battle, while Ricker calls the earlier action the opening fight.
assertions.limit: Editorial organization and participant framing differ; neither supplies an automatic segmentation rule. Preserve both interpretations.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.89; p89-april4
citations.quote: APRIL 4, 1862.—Skirmish near Pittsburg Landing, Tenn.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.93; p93-april6-7
citations.quote: APRIL 6–7, 1862.—Battle of Pittsburg Landing, or Shiloh, Tenn.

citations.locator: OR Series I, volume X, part 1, printed p.92; p92-ricker-framing
citations.quote: I acknowledge God's mercy in protecting our men under the terrible fire poured upon us by the enemy in the opening fight of the great battle of Pittsburg.

assertions.statement: Reed reports a Saturday engagement near Howell’s.
assertions.limit: Retrospective compilation; no participant source or continuous link to Sunday is established by this packet. A negative OCR search is not evidence of absence.

citations.locator: Reed, revised 1909, printed p.68, Third Corps paragraph
citations.quote: another engagement with a picket post near Howell's on Saturday

coverage.visual_scope: Selected passages and nearby context on 18 OR pages and Reed p.68; not every word or the whole source corpus.

segmentation_recommendation.anchor: Sustained assault episode documented on April 6; walk backward through linked contacts, including pickets and cavalry.
segmentation_recommendation.rule: Treat an earlier encounter as precursor where affirmative reports describe its termination/return and a subsequent approach or attack phase. Date change, overnight rest, quiet claims, intention, or editorial labeling alone are insufficient. Stop at an unresolved continuity link; do not silently exclude it.
segmentation_recommendation.scope: Opening segmentation only. No new battle-end boundary, cohort row, outcome, troop population, or operational/campaign score. This rule is defined after source inspection, not preregistered.

april3.limit: Earlier approach contacts; exact incidents may overlap and their local endings are not independently reconstructed. Classification rests on subsequent return/reset evidence, not each contact having its own documented end.

april4.limit: Preserves Ricker’s broader opening-fight interpretation as an alternative; no unanimous historical adjudication.

april5_howell.limit: Need underlying participant account, location/unit identity and termination or continuation evidence.

april6.limit: First shot, clock, extent and screen identity unresolved; no 4:55 adoption or reset to main-line advance.

segmentation_recommendation.alternative: A broader operation including April 3–7 remains a distinct research estimand; do not add its result to the battle as independent credit.

next_action: Trace Reed’s Howell claim through Shiloh park commission reports/tablet files and candidate participant accounts; preserve unknown if no underlying testimony can be inspected.
